A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Inheritune, and their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison. Retained algorithms and experiments can be matched despite substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original low-data language-model evaluations, GPT-2 training and downstream results, and initialization ablations, including Tables 3, 6 and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds attention diagnostics, initialization and distillation comparisons, GPT-2 xLarge results, and FineWeb-Edu evaluations.

M1.justification: v2 Algorithm 1 matches the iterative procedure already presented in v1 Algorithm 2: inherit early layers and embeddings/head, train, and increase depth until reference validation performance is matched. The fixed-depth low-data recipe from v1 Algorithm 1 survives in v2 Appendix B. The attention analysis supplies new motivation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds FineWeb-Edu training and evaluations on ARC-Easy, SciQ and HellaSwag in Section 5. RedPajama, OpenWebText and the earlier downstream coverage remain, including Wikitext and LAMBADA, which were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated stacking, hybrid-stacking and half-width baselines in Table 2, plus vanilla and teacher-initialized knowledge distillation in Figures 3 and 8. Figure 1 also compares late-layer initialization with early-layer and random initialization. The low-data comparison retains OPT, Pythia, MPT and Sheared LLaMA.

E3.justification: v2 introduces GPT-2 xLarge configurations, 10K-step layer-transfer tests, 50K-step distillation comparisons, attention-diagnostic protocols and 100K-step FineWeb-Edu training without repetition. For existing GPT-2 experiments, reported warmup changes from 1K to 2K steps and the Large learning rate from 3e-4 to 2e-4. These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds attention-rank and column-mass analyses, early-versus-late-layer transfer tests, attention visualizations and a FineWeb-Edu check of whether gains depend on data repetition. It removes v1's experiment without residual connections. Existing attention/MLP/layernorm ablations and low-data depth, epoch and token-repetition analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 1 introduces means and standard deviations over 100 sampled-sequence attention analyses; Figure 2 averages attention maps over three sampled strings. These concern diagnostic sampling, not independently repeated model training. Main performance tables still lack uncertainty estimates, while the earlier single-run checkpoint explanation is retained.

E6.justification: Existing GPT-2 Medium/Large and low-data table scores are retained, but v2 adds xLarge, initialization/distillation, attention and FineWeb-Edu results. For example, xLarge Inheritune reports validation loss 2.64 and LAMBADA 43.30; Table 2 shows a 2.64 tie with hybrid stacking despite claims of consistent outperformance. v1's no-residual result, loss 7.5 at 42K steps, is removed.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2 adds mathematical definitions for approximate attention rank using 90% singular-value energy and column concentration using 90% matrix mass. These formalize new diagnostics absent from v1. No new theorem or proof establishing Inheritune's properties is provided.

C1.justification: v2 adds the central claim that deeper-layer attention degenerates into uninformative 'lazy layers' and that Inheritune remedies this structural inefficiency. v1's main claims concerned token- and compute-efficient small-model training, whose evidence remains in Appendix B. v2 also claims superiority over newly evaluated initialization and distillation methods.

C2.justification: v2 interprets attention degeneration as explaining poor late-layer transfer and motivates smaller models through a new vanishing-gradient argument in Appendix A. It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning depth-only architectural changes and sensitivity to training-data quality. Section 4.1 newly acknowledges the xLarge exception where longer scratch training performs better.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix C substantially expands GPT-2 documentation: validation-set size, AdamW coefficients, activations, bias/dropout choices, attention scaling, distributed training, gradient accumulation and baseline configurations. Distillation temperature and loss weighting are specified, and Table 7 adds compute-resource information. The low-data hyperparameters and project code link are retained.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from low-data training, pruning and compression toward attention degeneration and model initialization. v2 adds substantial discussion of Dong, Noci, He, Barbero and Zhai, alongside stacking work by Gong, Reddi, Du and Agarwal. The detailed pruning/Sheared LLaMA discussion and associated citations are removed although its benchmark scores remain.

P1.justification: The title, author block, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively revised. An attention-centered narrative replaces the earlier low-data-first organization; the low-data study and implications move into Appendix B, the FAQ disappears, and implementation documentation is reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. New attention panels, heatmaps, distillation plots and comparison tables substantially alter the presentation. Earlier Figures 1–4 become appendix Figures 10–13, GPT-2 convergence displays are redrawn and expanded, and hyperparameter tables become lists.

improvement.justification: New initialization/distillation comparisons and FineWeb-Edu tests strengthen empirical support for the retained method, while Appendix C improves documentation. These gains are tempered by the stronger claim that lazy layers cannot learn, which the transfer diagnostics do not establish, removal of explicit limitations, and contradictory half-width baseline depths in Tables 2 and 10. The net improvement is therefore limited.
